rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans almost the full organic range so all 10 compounds are likely to elute and we can map the elution window and any missing late peaks. A mid temperature gives a balanced first look at retention and selectivity without making the run unnecessarily long.

All compounds are fully resolved already, so the only way to improve CRF is to pull the last peak earlier by trimming the gradient window to the observed elution range while keeping all peaks inside the gradient. Based on the first run, the peaks elute over roughly phi_e 0.11 to 0.41, so a narrower, slightly shifted window should preserve resolution and shorten t_last.

The narrower window increased retention, so the next lever to improve CRF is temperature: raising T should move all peaks earlier and may keep selectivity acceptable because current resolution margins are large. Using the original broad gradient isolates the temperature effect cleanly against the successful baseline run.

At 60 C all pairs still have comfortable resolution, so the best chance to raise CRF further is to steepen the gradient slightly and see if the last peak can be pushed under 10 min without losing full credit on the weakest pair. This directly tests how much resolution margin remains while targeting the time penalty.

The 16 min gradient got t_last below 10 min but slightly over-compressed the critical 4/5 pair; a small increase in tG should restore that pair toward full credit while likely keeping the last peak under 10 min. This is the most direct local optimization around the current best condition.

The tradeoff is now very tight: at 60 C and 18 min the critical pair is just shy of full resolution while the last peak is only 0.21 min late. Dropping temperature slightly should increase retention and likely improve the 4/5 selectivity enough to reach full resolution credit, with only a small risk of adding less time penalty than the resolution gain.

A small increase in phi0 changes the effective gradient window without repeating the current best method, which may improve selectivity around the critical 4/5 pair while also slightly shortening retention. The shift is modest enough that all compounds should still elute with strong overall resolution.

The critical pair is very sensitive to the effective phi window, and increasing phi0 hurt it; the next clean selectivity test is to keep the low starting strength but lower phi1 slightly. That changes gradient steepness and outlet phi around the 4/5 region with minimal impact on full elution, while the current best already shows only a tiny time penalty to recover.

Since the optimum seems to lie between the 16 min and 18 min behaviors, lowering phi1 while using the shorter 16 min gradient may recover the lost 4/5 resolution without giving up the favorable sub-10 min last peak too badly. This tests whether a small window compression can improve selectivity enough to outperform the current best tradeoff.

The critical pair responds strongly to temperature and slope, and 55 C shifted the weakest pair from 4/5 to 6/7. Testing 50 C at the current best gradient probes whether a further selectivity change can lift all pairs above 1.5 while only modestly increasing t_last from 10.21 min.

At 55 C the critical pair moved to 6/7, and at 18 min it was only slightly underresolved; lengthening the gradient should help that slope-sensitive pair more than it hurts the modest time penalty. This tests whether 55 C offers a better selectivity regime than 60 C once enough gradient time is given.

The best method is very close to ideal, and lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the 4/5 pair but made the last peak too late; one more small decrease in the upper endpoint tests whether selectivity can improve further enough to offset the extra retention. This is a focused probe of whether the critical pair benefits from a narrower high-organic limit.

Since 18 min is slightly too short for the 4/5 pair and 20 min is already known to give full resolution, moving longer tests whether the fully resolved regime has enough robustness to support later window changes, while also confirming the slope trend around the critical pair. This is a distinct point beyond the current bracket and may clarify whether 4/5 is still improving meaningfully with tG.

With 0.95 upper organic, 20 min gives full resolution but too much time penalty; lowering phi1 improved the critical 4/5 pair at 18 min, so trying that selectivity shift at 20 min tests whether the fully resolved condition can be kept while reducing the weakness around 4/5. This directly maps whether phi1 and tG trade off smoothly near the optimum.

The main unresolved question is whether a stronger selectivity shift in the upper endpoint can lift the 4/5 pair enough at the short, no-time-penalty gradient. A 16 min run with lower phi1 keeps pressure on t_last while probing whether that critical pair can cross 1.5 and beat the current best.

Lowering phi1 to 0.80 fully resolved the critical pair but made the run too long; shortening tG should pull t_last back toward 10 min while likely retaining enough 4/5 resolution because that pair had comfortable margin at this window. This is the most direct attempt to combine the selectivity advantage of phi1 0.80 with the time advantage of the shorter gradient.

At phi1 0.80 and 16 min, all pairs are resolved but the last peak is only modestly late; lowering temperature may improve the selectivity margin around the critical region more than enough to offset a small increase in t_last. This probes whether the narrower window changes the temperature dependence of the troublesome pair compared with the broad-window runs.

At 14 min and 60 C, lowering phi1 from 0.90 to 0.80 improved the critical 4/5 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so one more step to 0.75 tests whether that trend continues enough to beat the current best. This is a tight local exploration of the upper gradient endpoint under the best short-gradient regime found so far.

The 14 min, phi1 0.75 condition ties the current best, so the next step is to steepen slightly and test whether the last peak can be pulled below 10 min while preserving enough 4/5 resolution to gain overall CRF. This is the most promising local move because the resolution deficit at the tied best is very small.

The tied-best condition at phi1 0.75 and 14 min suggests we are on a ridge where the upper endpoint may be exchangeable with gradient time; lowering phi1 another step at the same tG tests whether the critical 4/5 pair can gain enough selectivity to cross 1.5 without worsening time beyond the tiny current penalty. This is a precise local probe around the best-performing narrow-window regime.

The tied-best point at phi1 0.75, 14 min likely sits just on the edge where the 4/5 pair is slightly under full credit; a small increase in tG is the cleanest way to lift that pair above 1.5. This tests whether the added resolution gain can outweigh the extra time penalty better than the broad-window 18 min method.

The data show a strong equivalence between shrinking phi1 and lengthening tG, and the best results sit where 4/5 is just under full credit with only a tiny time penalty. Moving to a narrower 0.65 endpoint with a shorter 12 min gradient targets the same balance but may shift the critical pair slightly more favorably while keeping t_last near 10 min.

Multiple conditions have collapsed to the same chromatogram, implying the separation is governed mainly by gradient steepness rather than the absolute upper endpoint. Stepping to a still shallower endpoint-time combination on that ridge may finally shift the 4/5 pair over full-credit resolution while holding the last peak close enough to 10 min to improve CRF.

The repeating patterns indicate many methods are effectively equivalent, but the best score still comes from the balance where the 4/5 pair is at R about 1.44 and t_last about 10.2 min. This untested endpoint-time combination preserves nearly the same overall steepness while shifting the absolute phi window slightly, giving one more chance to nudge 4/5 above 1.5 without adding much time.

The results show a family of equivalent methods where the key control is gradient steepness, and the best-achieved point sits just shy of full resolution on the 4/5 pair with only 0.21 min of time penalty. With one shot left, the best gamble is a slightly shallower step along that ridge, which could nudge 4/5 to full credit while keeping t_last close enough to 10 min to exceed 0.986.
